why: Prior freeze proved batch-count optimality + witness legality; cost-optimality rested on an A*-consistency argument scoped to 'no cheaper 4-/5-batch schedule'. A us-optimal schedule need NOT use the minimum batch count (per-batch transfer cost 2*15us/atom), so the scope was insufficient. This campaign settles it by Dijkstra over the FULL reachable state space with the frozen edge weight.
method: cdijkstra.c — batch legality/child generation is a line-for-line replica of the frozen gate-B cbfs.c gen(); edge weight = move_batch_duration_us(dmax) + 2*15us*|batch| (config.py); costs ordered in fixed point, quantum 2^-20 us; witness via parent chain
bug_found_and_fixed_in_this_campaign: First cdijkstra build had a sift-down that compared children against the vacated root instead of the relocated last element, destroying the heap invariant: pops came out unordered, states re-settled (533M settles vs 5.77M reachable) and n=3 returned 1003.54us/8 batches. Fixed; n=3 now 288.780458 us/3 batches == independent Python Dijkstra 288.78045748 (1e-6 agreement).
verdict: Both frozen cost rows are GLOBAL us optima over the full reachable 4x4 state space, to the 2^-20 us fixed-point quantum (n5 diff 1.1e-7 us, n6 diff 8.2e-7 us), with witnesses that replay exactly (<=5e-13 us) and whose batch counts equal the BFS diameters (4, 5). The 'consistent-A*' dependency is now DROPPED.
